## 6. EvaluationRecord structural contract

### 6.1 Snapshot versus sequence

**Preferred form:** a single-evaluation snapshot representing one completed
evaluation.

A sequence of evaluation events is not part of the CORE-001 MVP. If a caller needs
history, it retains a list of immutable snapshots. A validated record must not be
mutated.

### 6.2 Proposed record shape

Field names are illustrative; the information requirements are the contract.

```ts
interface EvaluationRecord {
  record_schema_version: string;     // e.g. "dec-06-evaluation-record@1"
  record_id: string;                 // identity of this record; unique within a record set
  evaluation_ref: EvaluationRef;     // identity of configuration/input tuple, not a unique execution ID

  input_set_ref: InputSetRef;        // binding to supplied Assessment set; not proof of completeness
  context_ref: ContextRef;           // id / version / digest
  policy_ref: PolicyRef;             // id / version / digest
  predicate_ref?: PredicateRef;      // absent when predicate_execution_status = NOT_CONFIGURED
  requirement_ref?: RequirementRef;  // optional; scope OPEN

  structural_candidates: AssessmentID[];

  // Canonical context facts. The sets context_applicable,
  // context_inapplicable, and context_unassessed are derived projections;
  // they are not stored as independent fields.
  context_disposition_facts: ContextDispositionFact[];

  considered: AssessmentID[];
  excluded_from_consideration: AssessmentID[];
  exclusion_facts: ExclusionFromConsiderationFact[];

  expected_pairs: PairRef[];
  pair_construction_mode: 'PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED' | 'RULE_SELECTED';
  pair_selection_rule_ref?: string;
  pair_selection_rule_version?: string;
  pair_selection_evidence_ref?: string;
  pair_evaluations: PairEvaluation[];   // sole authoritative pair-result source

  context_assessment_status: 'COMPLETE' | 'PARTIAL';
  pair_coverage_status: 'NO_PAIRS' | 'NOT_STARTED' | 'PARTIAL' | 'COVERED' | 'FAILED';
  predicate_execution_status: 'NOT_CONFIGURED' | 'NOT_INVOKED' | 'INVOKED' | 'INVOCATION_FAILED';

  pair_order: 'UNORDERED_CANONICAL' | 'ORDERED';
  symmetry_declaration: 'SYMMETRIC' | 'ASYMMETRIC' | 'UNSPECIFIED';
  symmetry_verification: {
    status: 'NOT_PERFORMED' | 'VERIFIED' | 'VIOLATION' | 'INCONCLUSIVE';
    mechanism_ref?: string;
    evidence_ref?: string;
  };
  symmetry_checks: SymmetryCheck[];

  claimed_origin: 'CORE_001' | 'EXTERNAL';
  origin_verification: {
    status: 'VERIFIED' | 'UNVERIFIED' | 'UNAVAILABLE';
    mechanism_ref?: string;
    evidence_ref?: string;
  };
  structural_validation: {
    status: 'PASSED' | 'FAILED' | 'NOT_PERFORMED';
    validator_ref?: string;
    evidence_ref?: string;
  };

  provenance?: DeclarationProvenance;
}
```

### 6.3 Context dispositions and derived sets

| Fact disposition | Derived set |
|---|---|
| `CONTEXT_APPLICABLE` | `context_applicable` |
| `CONTEXT_INAPPLICABLE` | `context_inapplicable` |
| `CONTEXT_UNASSESSED` | `context_unassessed` |

The record stores `context_disposition_facts`, not the three sets. The sets are
derived views:

```text
context_applicable   = { f.assessment_id | f.disposition = CONTEXT_APPLICABLE }
context_inapplicable = { f.assessment_id | f.disposition = CONTEXT_INAPPLICABLE }
context_unassessed   = { f.assessment_id | f.disposition = CONTEXT_UNASSESSED }
```

There is exactly one `ContextDispositionFact` per `structural_candidate`. Duplicate
facts are a structural error. A structural candidate with no fact makes the record
structurally invalid.

`context_assessment_status = COMPLETE` means every structural candidate has a fact
and no fact is `CONTEXT_UNASSESSED`. `PARTIAL` means every structural candidate has
a fact and at least one is `CONTEXT_UNASSESSED`. If `structural_candidates` is
empty, `COMPLETE` holds vacuously.

The context sets are pairwise disjoint and partition `structural_candidates` when
`CONTEXT_UNASSESSED` is retained. If `CONTEXT_UNASSESSED` is not retained, an
indeterminate candidate must not be placed in `context_inapplicable`; the record
must be marked structurally incomplete.

### 6.4 Context inapplicability versus exclusion

| State | Meaning | N3/N4 apply? | Governing obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_inapplicable` | Policy declares the Assessment outside the evaluation context | **No** — it is not "otherwise applicable" | N1/N5: criteria must be declared, versioned, not post-hoc |
| `excluded_from_consideration` | Assessment is context-applicable but not made available to the predicate | **Yes** — this is the "otherwise applicable" set | N3/N4: exclusion solely because of conflict is prohibited |
| `context_unassessed` | Applicability could not be determined | **No** | Record must not treat it as inapplicable; N1/N5 apply to criteria |

**Critical note:** N3/N4 do not close the loophole where a policy labels a
conflicting Assessment `context_inapplicable`. That state is governed by N1/N5 and
external judgment. The record makes the state visible; it does not prevent a
pretextual context criterion.

### 6.5 Input-set binding

`input_set_ref` identifies the actual Assessment input set supplied to the
evaluation. It may be:

- a reference to an immutable input manifest;
- a digest of a canonical serialisation of the set;
- both.

**What it establishes:** the record is bound to a specific supplied input set.

**What it does not establish:** that the supplied set was complete, that it
contained every domain-relevant Assessment, or that the policy did not omit an
Assessment before supplying it.

`structural_candidates` must be derived from the input set referenced by
`input_set_ref`.

For external records, validation of the relationship between `input_set_ref` and
recorded IDs requires at least one of:

- the actual input set or a manifest;
- a verifiable membership proof;
- a trusted external reference the validator can resolve.

A digest alone binds the record to the input but does not allow membership
validation without the set.

### 6.6 Disposition evidence contract

```ts
interface ContextDispositionFact {
  assessment_id: AssessmentID;
  disposition: 'CONTEXT_APPLICABLE' | 'CONTEXT_INAPPLICABLE' | 'CONTEXT_UNASSESSED';
  reason: string;
  rule_ref?: string;
  policy_ref?: PolicyRef;
  context_ref?: ContextRef;
  provenance?: string;
}

interface ExclusionFromConsiderationFact {
  assessment_id: AssessmentID;
  reason: string;
  rule_ref?: string;
  policy_ref?: PolicyRef;
  context_ref?: ContextRef;
  provenance?: string;
}
```

No exclusion taxonomy is approved. Facts preserve reason, reference, and
provenance; they do not prove the reason true.

### 6.7 Pair identity and expected coverage

#### PairRef and PairKey

```ts
interface PairRef {
  left: AssessmentID;
  right: AssessmentID;
}

type PairKey = string;

function pairKey(pair: PairRef, order: 'UNORDERED_CANONICAL' | 'ORDERED'): PairKey {
  if (order === 'UNORDERED_CANONICAL') {
    return `${min(pair.left, pair.right)}\u0000${max(pair.left, pair.right)}`;
  }
  return `${pair.left}\u0000${pair.right}`;
}
```

- In `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` mode, `(A, B)` and `(B, A)` have the same `PairKey`.
- In `ORDERED` mode, order is part of the key; reversed pairs are distinct.
- Duplicate expected pairs, duplicate pair evaluations, and reversed duplicates are
  detected by `PairKey`.
- Canonical ordering is ascending `PairKey`.
- Expected pairs in `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` are stored with `left < right`.

#### Construction modes

| Mode | Required rule fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` | None. `pair_selection_rule_ref`, `pair_selection_rule_version`, and `pair_selection_evidence_ref` MUST be absent | Expected pairs are every unordered distinct pair of `considered` |
| `RULE_SELECTED` | `pair_selection_rule_ref`, `pair_selection_rule_version`, and `pair_selection_evidence_ref` MUST be present | Expected pairs are the rule output |

For `RULE_SELECTED`:

- the rule input is `considered` plus the corresponding Assessment records resolved
  through `input_set_ref`, `context_ref`, and `policy_ref`;
- `pair_selection_evidence_ref` MUST resolve to an artifact that binds the rule
  version, the input reference, and the output `expected_pairs`;
- the rule must be declared and applied without reference to the conflict outcome
  (policy obligation; external judgment);
- the rule does not establish normative completeness of the expected pair universe.

The default `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` is **PROPOSED**.

#### Derived pair views

`pair_evaluations` is the sole authoritative source. The following are derived, not
stored:

```text
expectedKeys   = { pairKey(p, pair_order) | p ∈ expected_pairs }
terminal_pairs = { p ∈ pair_evaluations | p.status ∈ {CONFLICT, NO_CONFLICT} }
failed_pairs   = { p ∈ pair_evaluations | p.status = FAILED }
missing_pairs  = { e ∈ expected_pairs | pairKey(e, pair_order) ∉
                   { pairKey(p, pair_order) | p ∈ pair_evaluations } }
conflict_findings = projection of terminal_pairs where status = CONFLICT
```

`pair_evaluations` MUST NOT contain a pair whose key is not in `expectedKeys`.
Every expected pair appears at most once in `pair_evaluations`. The accounting
equation is:

```text
expected_pairs = terminal_pairs ⊎ failed_pairs ⊎ missing_pairs
```

where `⊎` is disjoint union.

#### Pair coverage statuses

| Status | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`NO_PAIRS`** | `expected_pairs` is empty |
| **`NOT_STARTED`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty and no expected pair appears in `pair_evaluations` |
| **`PARTIAL`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty; at least one expected pair is terminal; at least one is failed or missing |
| **`COVERED`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty; every expected pair is terminal; `missing_pairs` is empty; no `FAILED` pair |
| **`FAILED`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty; no expected pair is terminal; at least one expected pair is `FAILED` |

`PARTIAL` and `FAILED` are mutually exclusive and testable from the derived counts.

### 6.8 Predicate execution statuses

| Status | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`NOT_CONFIGURED`** | No predicate configured. `predicate_ref` is absent. No pair evaluations |
| **`NOT_INVOKED`** | Predicate configured (`predicate_ref` present), but no pair evaluation was attempted |
| **`INVOKED`** | At least one pair was attempted; no pair has status `FAILED` |
| **`INVOCATION_FAILED`** | At least one pair was attempted and has status `FAILED` |

**Derived `EXECUTED`:**

```text
EXECUTED iff predicate_execution_status = INVOKED
        and pair_coverage_status = COVERED
        and expected_pairs is non-empty
```

`EXECUTED` is a mechanism-coverage label. It does not establish semantic
correctness or successful conflict assessment when symmetry is `VIOLATION` or
`INCONCLUSIVE`.

**Missing predicate:** `NOT_CONFIGURED` must not require a `predicate_ref`.

**Context blocking:** represented as `predicate_execution_status = NOT_INVOKED` and
`pair_coverage_status = NOT_STARTED` (or `NO_PAIRS` if no pairs). It is never
`INVOCATION_FAILED`.

### 6.9 Pair evaluations, findings, and predicate references

```ts
interface PairEvaluation {
  left: AssessmentID;
  right: AssessmentID;
  status: 'CONFLICT' | 'NO_CONFLICT' | 'FAILED';
  claims?: readonly string[];
  reason?: string;
  predicate_ref: PredicateRef;
}
```

`pair_evaluations` is authoritative. `terminal_pairs`, `failed_pairs`,
`missing_pairs`, and `conflict_findings` are derived views, not stored fields. If a
serialised view is produced, it MUST equal the derivation exactly. `FAILED` and
`NO_CONFLICT` pairs produce no findings.

Top-level `predicate_ref` MUST equal every `PairEvaluation.predicate_ref` when
present, and MUST be absent when `predicate_execution_status = NOT_CONFIGURED`.

A Finding remains a detection result, not a Ruling or resolution.

### 6.10 Record schema, identity, and validation

| Field | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`record_schema_version`** | Identifies the record contract version (e.g. `dec-06-evaluation-record@1`). Not an evaluation identity |
| **`record_id`** | Identity of this record. Uniqueness is validated across a record set, not by inspecting an isolated record; not globally unique |
| **`evaluation_ref`** | Identity of the evaluation configuration/input tuple. Not a unique execution ID; repeated executions of the same configuration/input may share it |
| **`context_ref`** | Identity of the policy/context declaration |
| **`input_set_ref`** | Binding to the supplied input set; not proof of completeness |

**Acceptance rules:**

- `claimed_origin` is self-asserted; it proves nothing by itself.
- `origin_verification.status = VERIFIED` requires non-empty `mechanism_ref` and
  `evidence_ref` supported by that mechanism. If the mechanism is unavailable, use
  `UNAVAILABLE`.
- `structural_validation.status = PASSED` requires non-empty `validator_ref` and
  `evidence_ref`, and satisfaction of E1–E21. It establishes internal consistency
  only.
- `symmetry_verification.status = VERIFIED` requires the evidence defined in §6.11.
- The origin, structural, and symmetry references are distinct claims. A reference
  proves that evidence is identified, not that it is sufficient, complete, or
  legitimate.
- A record is **core-accepted** only if `claimed_origin = CORE_001`,
  `origin_verification.status = VERIFIED` by the core mechanism, and
  `structural_validation.status = PASSED`. This is **PROPOSED**.
- An external record may be `structurally_validated_external`; structural validation
  does not imply core origin, completeness, policy legitimacy, or predicate semantic
  correctness.

### 6.11 Symmetry verification

```ts
interface SymmetryCheck {
  left: AssessmentID;
  right: AssessmentID;
  forward_status: 'CONFLICT' | 'NO_CONFLICT' | 'FAILED';
  reverse_status: 'CONFLICT' | 'NO_CONFLICT' | 'FAILED';
  evidence_ref: string;
}
```

`comparison` is derived, not stored:

```text
comparison = MATCH          if forward_status and reverse_status are terminal and equal
             MISMATCH       if forward_status and reverse_status are terminal and differ
             INCONCLUSIVE   if either status is FAILED
```

**`symmetry_checks` invariants:**

- Every check references two distinct IDs in `expected_pairs`.
- No duplicate check for the same `PairKey`.
- `forward_status` MUST equal the corresponding `pair_evaluations` status.
- `reverse_status` is the result of the reverse-order evaluation.
- `comparison` is derived from the two statuses; a serialised value must match.
- `evidence_ref` is mandatory for every check that contributes to `VERIFIED`.
- `symmetry_checks` is a verification trace, not a second source of ordinary pair
  results.

**Symmetry statuses:**

| Status | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`NOT_PERFORMED`** | No checks and no mechanism guarantee |
| **`VERIFIED`** | Every expected pair is covered by a `MATCH` check with `evidence_ref`, or by a mechanism guarantee with `mechanism_ref` and `evidence_ref`; no `INCONCLUSIVE` or `MISMATCH` |
| **`VIOLATION`** | At least one `MISMATCH` |
| **`INCONCLUSIVE`** | Checks were performed, but coverage is partial or at least one comparison is `INCONCLUSIVE`, and no `MISMATCH` exists |

**Valid combinations:**

| `pair_order` | `symmetry_declaration` | Allowed `symmetry_verification.status` |
|---|---|---|
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `ASYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `ORDERED` | `ASYMMETRIC` or `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`; ordered semantics OPEN |
| `ORDERED` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE`; ordered semantics OPEN |

A single canonical evaluation of `(left, right)` cannot establish that
`(right, left)` produces the same result. Without reverse-order evidence or a
mechanism guarantee, `VERIFIED` is not permitted.

### 6.12 Structural invariants

| ID | Invariant |
|---|---|
| **E1** | No duplicate IDs within any single list |
| **E2** | `structural_candidates` contains only IDs present in the input set referenced by `input_set_ref` |
| **E3** | Context disposition facts are pairwise disjoint by `assessment_id` |
| **E4** | Every structural candidate has exactly one `ContextDispositionFact` |
| **E5** | `context_assessment_status = COMPLETE` implies all facts are `CONTEXT_APPLICABLE` or `CONTEXT_INAPPLICABLE`; `PARTIAL` implies at least one `CONTEXT_UNASSESSED` |
| **E6** | `considered` and `excluded_from_consideration` are disjoint subsets of the derived `context_applicable` set |
| **E7** | `considered` and `excluded_from_consideration` partition the derived `context_applicable` set |
| **E8** | Every `excluded_from_consideration` ID has an `ExclusionFromConsiderationFact` |
| **E9** | `PairKey` canonical ordering holds; no duplicate or reversed-duplicate keys in `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` mode |
| **E10** | `expected_pairs = terminal_pairs ⊎ failed_pairs ⊎ missing_pairs`; no extra pair evaluations |
| **E11** | `pair_evaluations` reference distinct IDs in `considered`; no duplicate `PairKey` |
| **E12** | `pair_coverage_status` matches the definitions in §6.7 |
| **E13** | `predicate_execution_status` matches the definitions in §6.8 |
| **E14** | Only the legal status combinations in §9.2 are permitted |
| **E15** | Derived `conflict_findings` equals the canonical `CONFLICT` projection of `pair_evaluations`; no stored duplicate may conflict with it |
| **E16** | `symmetry_verification.status = VERIFIED` requires `symmetry_checks` coverage and evidence, or a mechanism guarantee; `VIOLATION` and `INCONCLUSIVE` prevent a symmetry/success claim |
| **E17** | `record_schema_version`, `record_id`, `evaluation_ref`, `input_set_ref`, `context_ref`, and `policy_ref` are present; `record_id` uniqueness is validated at record-set level |
| **E18** | No winner, preferred, canonical, resolved, selected-branch, or resolution field is present |
| **E19** | `origin_verification.status = VERIFIED` requires non-empty `mechanism_ref` and `evidence_ref`; `structural_validation.status = PASSED` requires non-empty `validator_ref` and `evidence_ref` |
| **E20** | `pair_construction_mode = PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` implies no selection-rule refs; `RULE_SELECTED` implies rule ref, version, and evidence ref are present, and the evidence binds rule version, input, and output |
| **E21** | Top-level `predicate_ref` equals every `PairEvaluation.predicate_ref` when present; it is absent when `predicate_execution_status = NOT_CONFIGURED` |

### 6.13 Validation limits

Structural validation establishes internal consistency only. It does not prove:

- completeness of the supplied input;
- that `context_inapplicable` is legitimate;
- that `excluded_from_consideration` is non-pretextual;
- that the expected pair universe is normatively complete;
- that the predicate is semantically correct;
- that the record represents what actually happened.

## 7. Predicate contract and limitations

### 7.1 Four distinct properties

| Property | Meaning | CORE-001 guarantee | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Declared inputs** | Input tuple is declared and recorded; includes both Assessment records or declared content, not merely IDs | Can constrain and record call signature | **PROPOSED** |
| **Deterministic execution** | Same declared inputs/context produce the same verdict | Can require and test for a pure function given declared inputs | **PROPOSED** |
| **Access isolation** | No closures, globals, ambient state, or other Assessments | Signature alone cannot guarantee; isolated execution or declarative predicates needed | **OPEN** |
| **Semantic correctness** | Predicate correctly captures the domain's contradiction concept | Not guaranteed; separate verification/normative judgment needed | **OPEN** |

### 7.2 Expected pair universe

- Current implementation evaluates all unordered distinct pairs of the set passed
  to `collectContestedClaims`, one canonical order per pair. This is implementation
  behaviour, not a normative definition.
- CORE-001 Rev 0.3.3 does not define the expected pair universe; **OPEN**.
- Default proposed construction: `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` (§6.7).
- Rule-selected subset: `pair_construction_mode = RULE_SELECTED`; rule ref, version,
  and evidence ref required; normative status **OPEN**.
- Atomic evaluation: not current behaviour; **PROPOSED/OPEN**. If adopted, per-pair
  findings must be preserved or marked unavailable.

### 7.3 Pair ordering and symmetry

- `pair_order` and `symmetry_declaration` are required.
- `symmetry_verification.status` records evidence, not a claim.
- A single canonical evaluation does not verify reversal invariance.
- `VERIFIED` requires reverse-order evidence or a verifiable mechanism guarantee.
- `VIOLATION` and `INCONCLUSIVE` prevent a symmetry claim and a successful
  symmetric conflict assessment claim.
- `ORDERED` semantics remain **OPEN**.

### 7.4 Partial failure and zero-pair semantics

| Situation | Coverage | Predicate | Success claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zero/one considered Assessment | `NO_PAIRS` | `NOT_CONFIGURED` or `NOT_INVOKED` | None |
| Expected pairs, no predicate | `NOT_STARTED` or `NO_PAIRS` | `NOT_CONFIGURED` | None |
| Expected pairs, configured, not attempted | `NOT_STARTED` | `NOT_INVOKED` | None |
| Some terminal, some failed/missing | `PARTIAL` | `INVOKED` or `INVOCATION_FAILED` | None |
| All expected terminal | `COVERED` | `INVOKED` | `EXECUTED` (mechanism) |
| No terminal, at least one failed | `FAILED` | `INVOCATION_FAILED` | None |

`PARTIAL` and `FAILED` are coverage statuses; they are not predicate statuses.
`NO_PAIRS` is a coverage status; it is not a predicate result.

### 7.5 Mechanism requirements

- Stable predicate identity/version.
- Declared input tuple.
- Both Assessment records or declared content.
- Deterministic behaviour for declared inputs.
- Immutable context; no mutation.
- Defined error/non-boolean behaviour maps to `INVOCATION_FAILED`.
- Pair ordering and symmetry declaration/verification recorded.
- Expected pair universe and selection rule recorded.
- No implicit majority, winner, or resolution.
- Per-pair and coverage statuses recorded.

### 7.6 Limits

A declared signature does not prevent closure over the full Assessment list,
globals, a clock, or mutable state. The core can constrain arguments, not prove
isolation. A deterministic, pure, versioned predicate can still be semantically
wrong.

A conflict finding means the configured predicate reported a conflict. It does not
prove contradiction. Absence of a finding does not prove no contradiction.
`NO_PAIRS` means no pair was evaluated; it does not prove no conflict.

**A-8 remains OPEN.** No invariant or test may assert which status wins when

### 9.2 Pair coverage × predicate execution combinations

Rows: `pair_coverage_status`. Columns: `predicate_execution_status`.

| Coverage \ Predicate | `NOT_CONFIGURED` | `NOT_INVOKED` | `INVOKED` | `INVOCATION_FAILED` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`NO_PAIRS`** | **Allowed.** No predicate, no pairs. No success claim | **Allowed.** Configured, no pairs. No success claim | **Forbidden.** Invocation implies pairs | **Forbidden.** Failure implies attempted pairs |
| **`NOT_STARTED`** | **Allowed.** Expected pairs exist, no predicate, no attempt. No success claim | **Allowed.** Configured, expected pairs, no attempt (e.g. context blocking). No success claim | **Forbidden.** Invocation implies attempted pairs | **Forbidden.** Failure implies attempted pairs |
| **`PARTIAL`** | **Forbidden.** No predicate cannot yield terminal pairs | **Forbidden.** No invocation cannot yield terminal pairs | **Allowed.** Some terminal, some missing. No full success claim | **Allowed.** Some terminal, some failed/missing. No full success claim |
| **`COVERED`** | **Forbidden.** No predicate cannot cover pairs | **Forbidden.** No invocation cannot cover pairs | **Allowed.** `EXECUTED` mechanism label; semantic success separate | **Forbidden.** A failed pair prevents coverage |
| **`FAILED`** | **Forbidden.** No predicate cannot produce failed pairs | **Forbidden.** No invocation cannot produce failed pairs | **Forbidden.** `INVOKED` requires no failed pairs | **Allowed.** No terminal, at least one failed. No success claim |

**Derived label:** `EXECUTED` iff `predicate_execution_status = INVOKED`,
`pair_coverage_status = COVERED`, and `expected_pairs` is non-empty. `EXECUTED` is
a mechanism-coverage label, not a semantic-correctness claim.

**Zero-pair rule:** `NO_PAIRS` can combine only with `NOT_CONFIGURED` or
`NOT_INVOKED`. It never implies success or absence of conflict.

**Context blocking rule:** context blocking uses `context_assessment_status =
PARTIAL` with `predicate_execution_status = NOT_INVOKED` and
`pair_coverage_status = NOT_STARTED` or `NO_PAIRS`. It is never
`INVOCATION_FAILED`.

**Missing predicate rule:** `NOT_CONFIGURED` requires `predicate_ref` to be absent.
`NO_PAIRS` or `NOT_STARTED` are the only legal coverage statuses with it.

- `symmetry_checks` is a verification trace, not a second source of ordinary pair
  results.

**Symmetry statuses:**

| Status | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`NOT_PERFORMED`** | No checks and no mechanism guarantee |
| **`VERIFIED`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty and every expected pair is covered by a `MATCH` check with `evidence_ref`, or by a mechanism guarantee with `mechanism_ref` and `evidence_ref`; no `INCONCLUSIVE` or `MISMATCH` |
| **`VIOLATION`** | At least one `MISMATCH` |
| **`INCONCLUSIVE`** | Checks were performed, but coverage is partial or at least one comparison is `INCONCLUSIVE`, and no `MISMATCH` exists |

When `expected_pairs` is empty, `symmetry_verification.status` MUST be `NOT_PERFORMED`; it cannot be `VERIFIED` vacuously.

**Valid combinations:**

| `pair_order` | `symmetry_declaration` | Allowed `symmetry_verification.status` |
|---|---|---|
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `ASYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `ORDERED` | `ASYMMETRIC` or `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`; ordered semantics OPEN |
| `ORDERED` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE`; ordered semantics OPEN |

A single canonical evaluation of `(left, right)` cannot establish that
`(right, left)` produces the same result. Without reverse-order evidence or a
mechanism guarantee, `VERIFIED` is not permitted.

### 6.12 Structural invariants

| ID | Invariant |
|---|---|
| **E1** | No duplicate IDs within any single list |
| **E2** | `structural_candidates` contains only IDs present in the input set referenced by `input_set_ref` |
| **E3** | Context disposition facts are pairwise disjoint by `assessment_id` |
| **E4** | Every structural candidate has exactly one `ContextDispositionFact` |

**Zero-pair rule:** `NO_PAIRS` can combine only with `NOT_CONFIGURED` or
`NOT_INVOKED`. It never implies success or absence of conflict.

**Context blocking rule:** context blocking uses `context_assessment_status =
PARTIAL` with `predicate_execution_status = NOT_INVOKED` and
`pair_coverage_status = NOT_STARTED` or `NO_PAIRS`. It is never
`INVOCATION_FAILED`.

**Missing predicate rule:** `NOT_CONFIGURED` requires `predicate_ref` to be absent.
`NO_PAIRS` or `NOT_STARTED` are the only legal coverage statuses with it.

### 9.3 Symmetry status combinations

| `pair_order` | `symmetry_declaration` | Legal `symmetry_verification.status` |
|---|---|---|
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `ASYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `ORDERED` | `ASYMMETRIC` or `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`; ordered semantics OPEN |
| `ORDERED` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `INCONCLUSIVE`; ordered semantics OPEN |

`VERIFIED` requires full expected-pair coverage by `MATCH` checks with evidence, or
a mechanism guarantee with distinct `mechanism_ref` and `evidence_ref`. `VIOLATION`
requires at least one `MISMATCH`. `INCONCLUSIVE` covers partial coverage or a
check with a `FAILED` side. A single canonical evaluation is never `VERIFIED`.

### 9.4 Invariant matrix

| Invariant | Check | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|

{"body":"# Independent Adversarial Review — DEC-06 / CORE-001 (PR #63, Addendum v2.5)

**Reviewer:** independent (not a continuation of the authors' design loop)
**Subject:** https://github.com/zaebee/federation-agents/pull/63 — `dec-06-owner-decision-addendum-v2.5.md` (new, 937 lines) + one-line pointer rows in `README.md` and `dec-06-contradictory-assessments.md`
**Basis reviewed:** full PR diff; surrounding `dec-06-contradictory-assessments.md` package; CORE-001 §6.2–§6.4, §8.5, §8.8; implementation coverage in `src/core/assessment.ts` / `src/core/traversal.ts`; both existing Gemini Code Assist comments (independently confirmed; see F-3, F-4).

---

## 1. Verdict

**`ACCEPT WITH OPEN ITEMS`**

The addendum's governance posture is honest: the three-layer conformance distinction (§3.1), the limits disclosures (§6.5, §6.13, §7.6), the preserved PROPOSED/OPEN/PENDING-SPEC-AMENDMENT statuses, and the O-1..O-3 / EP-2 / BP-1 requirement of explicit owner decisions all survive adversarial inspection, and no OPEN decision is silently resolved. The proposed record contract itself, however, is not self-consistent: the expected pair universe is indeterminate in ORDERED mode (F-1), one legitimate symmetry-evaluation outcome has no representable status (F-2), and the `pairKey`/E10 accounting carries a type mismatch, an undeclared collision risk, and a per-evaluation predicate-identity gap (F-3–F-5). Mandatory checks 2, 3 and 7 fail as written and 1, 4, 5, 8 pass only partially; these are contract-drafting defects fixable by technical editing, not architecture, but the document must not be adopted as the EvaluationRecord baseline until they are corrected.

---

## 2. Findings

### F-1 — HIGH — `pair_order = ORDERED` + `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED`: expected pair universe indeterminate; `SymmetryCheck` ↔ `pair_evaluations` mapping undefined in ORDERED mode

- **Sections:** §6.7 ("Expected pairs are every *unordered* distinct pair of `considered`"); §6.11; E9–E11; §9.2/§9.3; S23.
- **Counterexample:** `considered = {X, Y}`, mode `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED`, `pair_order = ORDERED`. §6.7 defines the universe as "every unordered distinct pair", so validator A correctly builds `expected_pairs = {(X,Y)}` while validator B correctly builds `{(X,Y),(Y,X)}` — S23 itself treats `(B,A)` as a distinct key under ORDERED. Both records satisfy E9–E11 and E14; no storage-orientation rule for ordered expected pairs exists (the `left < right` rule is stated only for `UNORDERED_CANONICAL`). Between the two readings, missing-pair derivation and `pair_coverage_status` differ by a factor of two; the contract cannot tell whether record A omitted an evaluation.
- **Second gap:** under ORDERED, `pairKey(B,A)` is a genuine expected pair, so its reverse result is legitimately a `pair_evaluations` entry — yet §6.11 only states "`forward_status` MUST equal the corresponding `pair_evaluations` status" and does not define whether/how `reverse_status` reconciles with that separate entry. The same execution then has two stored status locations with no invariant tying them; a divergent `reverse_status` makes a conflict finding's truth assessment depend on which source is consulted.
- **Why it matters:** the expected pair universe feeds every coverage status, `EXECUTED`, and deriveable findings; two equally conformant constructions mean status is derived partly from the record author's choice, not from evidence.
- **Classification:** contract defect. The document only isolates the problem with the "ordered semantics OPEN" notes; "OPEN" does not make E9–E11 well-defined over both readings.
- **Minimum fix:** prohibit the combination explicitly, or define the ordered expected universe (orientation enumeration and storage rule) and the ORDERED mapping of `SymmetryCheck` to `pair_evaluations` entries.

### F-2 — HIGH — Unrepresentable state: a fully MATCHed reverse evaluation under `symmetry_declaration = UNSPECIFIED` has no legal `symmetry_verification.status`

S19's phrase "findings non-authoritative" contradicts §6.9's canonical-source principle; at best it means "no complete-evaluation success claim", but as written it invites callers to discard legitimate partial findings.
- **Why it matters:** the sole-source principle (C-6, E15) is the fix for prior duplicate-source defects; S19's wording reintroduces ambiguity at its edge case.
- **Classification:** contract defect (wording); one-line correction.
- **Minimum fix:** reword S19: "pair_evaluations remains authoritative per pair; no complete-coverage success claim arises."

### F-9 — LOW — Approval provenance: §1 "the approved direction" and §11 T-1 "APPROVED constraint" cite approvals that no shown record establishes

- **Sections:** §1 line 29–31; §4.1; §11 T-1.
- **Counterexample:** the document's own header declares `PROPOSED — no new approval`, §2 says "no new proposal is APPROVED", yet §4.1 asserts "The owner has approved Evidence Preservation, Branch Preservation, and No Implicit Reconciliation" without citing which decision record contains that approval, and T-1 is marked `APPROVED constraint`. Whether these trace to a real prior decision or silently upgrade earlier PROPOSED principles cannot be established from the package — precisely the "implicit approval" the registration rules forbid.
- **Why it matters:** the same mechanism the addendum uses to protect every other decision (explicit status with provenance) is missing for the three claims that anchor the whole responsibility table in §4.5.
- **Classification:** owner decision needed (declare the provenance) or contract edit (link the decision record id); not silently resolvable.
- **Minimum fix:** cite the decision artifact/version approving those principles, or re-mark them PROPOSED for consistency.

### F-10 — LOW — `RULE_SELECTED`: no invariant constrains `expected_pairs` ⊆ pairs(`considered`)

- **Sections:** §6.7 `RULE_SELECTED` bullet list vs E11.
- **Counterexample:** rule emits an expected pair over two `excluded_from_consideration` assessments; that pair is never evaluated. E10 balances (missing pair), E11 is satisfied (no evaluations exist), the record is valid, yet the declared rule input ("`considered` plus the corresponding Assessment records") and its output disagree — detectable from the record, but not prohibited.
- **Why it matters:** bidirectional asymmetry: evaluated pairs are constrained to `considered`, expected pairs are not; either constrain them or state that rule output may target the wider context-applicable set (a different normative claim).
- **Classification:** contract defect (small).
- **Minimum fix:** one clause in E20/E11 binding `RULE_SELECTED` output to the declared rule-input scope.

### F-11 — LOW — `origin_verification.status = VERIFIED` is only attestation-grade; E19 validates ref non-emptiness, not evidence relevance

- **Sections:** §6.10 acceptance rules; E19; mandatory check 8.
- **Counterexample:** `claimed_origin = CORE_001`, `origin_verification = {status: VERIFIED, mechanism_ref: "mer-1", evidence_ref: "ref-x"}` where `ref-x` is irrelevant or unresolvable. A structural validator passes E19; "supported by that mechanism" is checkable only by resolving out-of-band references, which the contract places outside structural validation (§6.10, §6.5). Detection of the false claim is impossible from the record alone.
- **Why it matters:** the `claimed_origin` (self-asserted) vs `origin_verification` (verified) distinction is real and well drawn, but the VERIFIED status still implies more than any structural check can establish; the honest framing exists in prose but the invariant checklist (§9.4) does not carry the limit.
- **Classification:** intentional limitation that needs an explicit label, not a redesign.
- **Minimum fix:** in E19/§9.4 add: "`VERIFIED`/`PASSED` are producer attestations; the structural check establishes non-emptiness only" — the same discipline the record already applies elsewhere.

---

- Structural invariants E1–E21, subject to the fixes above; status combination legality (§9.2, §9.3); consistency between declared statuses and recorded facts; uniqueness/disjointness; pair accounting by `PairKey`; presence/equality of identity and predicate references (after F-5).
- Not checkable from the record under the current text (each anchored above): E10 equality semantics (F-4), the ORDERED expected universe (F-1), the `VERIFIED`-via-mechanism branch (F-6), and evidence-reference relevance for origin/structural/symmetry claims (F-11, §6.5).

### Receiving-domain policy (obligations on policy, judged externally)

- Input completeness; the legitimacy, non-pretextuality and pre-declaration of context criteria and exclusion reasons (N1/N3/N4/N5, D2/D3); the conflict-freeness of `RULE_SELECTED` rule design ("the rule must be declared and applied without reference to the conflict outcome", §6.7); the normative completeness of the expected pair universe.
- Note: as written, these obligations carry no normative force yet — N3/N4 are PROPOSED additions, N5 is PENDING SPEC AMENDMENT, and D3's legitimacy standard is OPEN. Policy conformance to them is *prospective*, not established by this document.

### External normative judgment (outside the contract entirely)

- Whether a `context_inapplicable` label is pretextual (S1/S16, O-PRETEXT); predicate semantic correctness (O-SEM); set-level vs pairwise contradiction (O-SET); A-8 precedence (O-A8); resolution authority and caller comparability (O-RES, O-CALLER); EP-2/BP-1 legitimacy (O-EPBP).

### Overclaim check on statements

- §3.2's guarantee table and §6.13 are accurate and are the honest core of the document.
- Overclaim instances found: `symmetry_verification.status = VERIFIED` via mechanism guarantee (F-6); `origin_verification.status = VERIFIED` presented as more than an attestation (F-11, moderate); S19's "findings non-authoritative" phrasing implying findings may be discarded (F-8); E16 as written being verifiable only in its MATCH-checks branch, not in the mechanism-guarantee branch (F-6).
- No statement found that overclaims set-level consistency, input completeness, policy legitimacy, or resolution — those limits are stated repeatedly and correctly.

---

## 4. Counterexample ledger (mandated adversarial cases)

|---|---|---|---|---|

2. **O-2 / O-3 — EP-2 and BP-1 adoption**, including the explicit boundary statement §4.5 presupposes; also the F-9 provenance question of which record already approved the three principles.

# Independent Adversarial Review — PR 63 (DEC-06 / CORE-001)

Source reviewed: `docs/.../dec-06-owner-decision-addendum-v2.5.md` (937 lines), plus `README.md` and `dec-06-contradictory-assessments.md`. Review is of the proposed contract text; no files were changed.

## 1. Verdict

**ACCEPT WITH OPEN ITEMS**

The addendum is a coherent, honestly bounded proposal and improves structural consistency over v2.3/v2.4, but it still contains concrete contract defects that must be corrected before it can support implementation or normative citation. The defects are local and correctable, yet several of them affect identity, coverage accounting, symmetry semantics, and predicate provenance. The document also leaves many decisions intentionally OPEN; those are not defects but they prevent implementation planning. No approval or merge is implied.

## 2. Findings

### F-01 — `pairKey()` comparator and delimiter encoding are undefined
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.7 `PairRef and PairKey`, function `pairKey`; E9.
- **Concrete counterexample:** `AssessmentID` values are treated as strings in the pseudo-code, but `min(pair.left, pair.right)` and `max(...)` are not defined for strings. Also, if IDs may contain U+0000, then `left\^@right` is not injective: `("a", "b\^@c")` and `("a\^@b", "c")` produce the same key.
- **Why it matters:** Pair identity, duplicate detection, missing-pair derivation, and symmetry checks all depend on `PairKey`; an unspecified comparator or non-injective encoding makes the contract untestable and allows silent key collisions.
- **Classification:** Contract defect.
- **Minimum correction:** Define the AssessmentID ordering used for canonicalisation (e.g. lexicographic by UTF-16 code unit / Unicode code point), state that U+0000 is forbidden in AssessmentID or use an escaping/length-prefixed encoding, and define `min`/`max` explicitly.

### F-02 — E10 disjoint-union equation mixes incompatible set types
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.7 `Derived pair views`, equation `expected_pairs = terminal_pairs ⊎ failed_pairs ⊎ missing_pairs`; E10.
- **Concrete counterexample:** `expected_pairs` is `PairRef[]`, while `terminal_pairs` and `failed_pairs` are sets of `PairEvaluation`, and `missing_pairs` is a subset of `expected_pairs`. The equation as written is not type-consistent and cannot be checked directly.
- **Why it matters:** The coverage oracle has two incompatible readings (by pair reference vs. by evaluation record), so tests cannot know whether an extra evaluation invalidates the record.
- **Classification:** Contract defect.
- **Minimum correction:** Rewrite the equation in `PairKey` terms, e.g. `expectedKeys = terminalKeys ⊎ failedKeys ⊎ missingKeys`, with each projection explicitly defined; or define `terminal_pairs`/`failed_pairs` as derived `PairRef` sets.

### F-03 — `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` is not compatible with `pair_order = ORDERED` as written
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.7 construction modes (`PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED`: “every unordered distinct pair”); §6.12 E9/E10; §9.3.
- **Concrete counterexample:** With `pair_order = ORDERED`, a caller could set `pair_construction_mode = PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED`. The mode generates one unordered pair per distinct ID pair, but ORDERED treats `(A,B)` and `(B,A)` as distinct keys. It is unspecified whether reverse orientations are expected, and therefore whether a symmetry check for `(A,B)` has an expected reversed pair.
- **Why it matters:** Pair coverage and reverse-order symmetry evidence cannot be derived for this combination; it risks either overcounting or silently dropping reverse checks.
- **Classification:** Contract defect (or explicit owner decision).
- **Minimum correction:** Either explicitly prohibit `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` when `pair_order = ORDERED`, or define its generated orientation set and how reverse-order pairs enter `expected_pairs`.

### F-04 — `SymmetryCheck` reverse-order mapping is ambiguous
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.11 `SymmetryCheck`; invariants “Every check references two distinct IDs in `expected_pairs`”, “`forward_status` MUST equal the corresponding `pair_evaluations` status”; §6.9.
- **Concrete counterexample:** In UNORDERED_CANONICAL mode, `(A,B)` and `(B,A)` share one key and only the canonical orientation appears in `pair_evaluations`; the reverse result exists only inside `SymmetryCheck`. In ORDERED mode, if only `(A,B)` is expected, `reverse_status` for `(A,B)` has no corresponding `PairEvaluation`. The text does not say how a failed reverse check is represented outside the trace, or whether both orientations must be expected in ORDERED mode.
- **Why it matters:** A validator cannot tell whether a `SymmetryCheck` is complete, whether its reverse status is independently supported, or whether `VERIFIED` is justified.
- **Classification:** Contract defect.
- **Minimum correction:** Specify reverse-status evidence requirements, state that reverse results are trace-only unless the reversed pair is itself an expected pair, and define expected-pairs membership for checks in both modes.

### F-05 — `VIOLATION` is allowed for `UNSPECIFIED` symmetry, conflating observed asymmetry with a violated declaration
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.11 valid combinations table; §9.3; `symmetry_verification.status = VIOLATION`.
- **Concrete counterexample:** `symmetry_declaration = UNSPECIFIED`, but forward evaluation is `CONFLICT` and reverse evaluation is `NO_CONFLICT`. The predicate is order-dependent, but no symmetry was declared; reporting `VIOLATION` implies a declared expectation was broken.
- **Why it matters:** This overclaims a guarantee and lets an observed implementation property be presented as a normative violation.
- **Classification:** Contract defect.
- **Minimum correction:** Restrict `VIOLATION` to `symmetry_declaration = SYMMETRIC`, or introduce a distinct status for observed order-dependence and update E16/§9.3 accordingly.

### F-06 — Top-level `predicate_ref` is not mandatory when pair evaluations exist
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.9 “Top-level `predicate_ref` MUST equal every `PairEvaluation.predicate_ref` when present”; E21; record shape `predicate_ref?`.
- **Concrete counterexample:** A record contains non-empty `pair_evaluations`, each with `predicate_ref`, but the top-level `predicate_ref` is omitted. E21 only requires equality “when present,” so the record can be structurally valid while failing to identify the predicate that produced the findings.
- **Why it matters:** The record can be internally consistent while omitting the identity of the mechanism behind its findings, weakening provenance and comparability.
- **Classification:** Contract defect.
- **Minimum correction:** Make top-level `predicate_ref` mandatory whenever `pair_evaluations` is non-empty (and absent only for `NOT_CONFIGURED`), and update E21 to require presence, not merely equality.

### F-07 — Origin, structural, and symmetry evidence references are not required to be distinct
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.10 acceptance rules; E19; §6.11 `evidence_ref`.
- **Concrete counterexample:** The same `evidence_ref` value is supplied for `origin_verification`, `structural_validation`, and `symmetry_verification`. Each object is non-empty, but one artifact cannot substantiate three separate claims.
- **Why it matters:** The separation of references is the point of B3; without a distinctness rule, the separation is cosmetic and cannot support the specific claim each object is meant to identify.
- **Classification:** Contract defect.
- **Minimum correction:** Require that evidence references (and mechanism/validator references) for origin, structural validation, and symmetry are not reused across those claims unless the contract defines a legitimate shared-evidence case.

### F-08 — Partial-failure semantics do not state that terminal findings remain authoritative
- **Severity:** MEDIUM
- **Exact section/field/invariant:** §6.8/§7.4 partial failure rows; §6.9 findings; S19.
- **Concrete counterexample:** Some expected pairs are `CONFLICT`/`NO_CONFLICT`, others are `FAILED`. §7.4 says no success claim, but S19 describes findings as “non-authoritative” without defining whether the successfully evaluated pairs’ findings are still valid detection results.
- **Why it matters:** Implementers may discard valid terminal findings after a partial failure, or conversely treat partial output as a complete result.
- **Classification:** Contract defect (clarity).
- **Minimum correction:** State explicitly that terminal pair findings remain authoritative detection results, while partial coverage prevents `EXECUTED` and any completeness/success claim.

Both Gemini Code Assist comments are confirmed independently: F-01 (`pairKey`) and F-02 (E10 disjoint-union type mismatch).

## 3. Guarantee boundary

**Guaranteed mechanically by the contract (where implemented and validated):**
- Structural candidate derivation from the supplied input set (one-way; not completeness).
- Disjoint context disposition facts and derived context sets.
- Considered/excluded partition of the derived applicable set.
- Pair identity, duplicate/reversed-duplicate detection, expected/terminal/failed/missing accounting.
- Pair coverage and predicate execution status derivability.
- Recording of configured predicate results and derived conflict findings.
- Distinction between detection, ruling, and resolution.
- Structural validation of internal consistency only.

**Required from receiving-domain policy (not provable by the core):**
- Completeness and legitimacy of supplied Assessments and context criteria.
- Non-pretextual context inapplicability and exclusion.
- Predicate semantic correctness.
- Conflict-handling and non-suppression obligations (N3/N4).
- Independence and versioning of context criteria (N1/N5).

**External normative judgment:**
- Legitimacy, appropriateness, and authority of policy.
- Whether a context criterion is a pretext.
- Resolution authority and representation.
- Comparability/substitutability of evaluations.

**Documented intentional limitations (not defects):**
- A structurally valid record may omit an Assessment that should have been in the domain-relevant input; `input_set_ref` binds supplied input, not completeness.
- `context_inapplicable` can be used to remove a conflicting Assessment from conflict detection; N3/N4 do not apply to that state, and the core records but does not prevent it.
- Pairwise evaluation may miss set-level inconsistency (O-SET).
- Determinism is required but access isolation is not guaranteed (O-ISO).
- Caller-side selection among multiple records is outside CORE-001 (O-CALLER).

**Statements that overclaim or need care:**
- `VIOLATION` under `UNSPECIFIED` (F-05) overstates a violated symmetry expectation.
- `context_assessment_status = COMPLETE` could be read as completeness of context determination; it is completeness only over the supplied structural candidates.
- `EXECUTED` is a mechanism-coverage label and must not be read as semantic correctness (the document says this, but it is a likely misread).

## 4. Unresolved owner decisions

These cannot be settled by editing the technical contract alone:

- EP-2 vs stronger Evidence Preservation scope (O-2).
- BP-1 vs core branch preservation/selection (O-3, O-BP).
- Conflict scope: edge vs declaration/subject (O-EDGE).
- Pre- vs post-narrowing conflict detection (§7.2).
- `contestedClaims` diagnostic content (§7.3, O-EMPTY).
- Conflict vs missing/disallowed precedence (O-A8).
- Whether a predicate is required to claim §6.4 support (§7.5, O-7).
- Ordered pair semantics and symmetry verification standard (O-SYM, O-PAIR).
- Access isolation mechanism (O-ISO).
- Authenticated origin mechanism (O-ORIGIN).

## 5. Release recommendation

**Specification review only.**  
The PR is suitable for specification review and as a decision-support artifact. It is not yet suitable for implementation planning until F-01–F-08 are corrected and the owner decisions in §4 are resolved; it is not suitable for implementation.

- S19 “findings non-authoritative” противоречит тому, что `pair_evaluations` — authoritative per-pair source.

- `origin_verification=VERIFIED` / `structural_validation=PASSED` — attestation-grade; E19 проверяет только непустоту refs.
- `context_assessment_status=COMPLETE` легко прочитать как полноту контекста, хотя это полнота только по supplied structural candidates.

CI зелёный, Sonar зелёный, но **merge не делал** и не рекомендую до исправлений. Сейчас PR — хороший decision-support артефакт, но не baseline для implementation.

- Every check references two distinct IDs in `expected_pairs`.
- No duplicate check for the same `PairKey`.
- `forward_status` MUST equal the corresponding canonical-order `pair_evaluations` status.
- `reverse_status` is trace-only unless the reversed pair is itself an expected
  pair (possible only with `RULE_SELECTED` + `ORDERED`); in that case it MUST equal
  that pair's `pair_evaluations` status.
- `comparison` is derived from the two statuses; a serialised value must match.
- `evidence_ref` is mandatory for every check that contributes to `VERIFIED`,
  `OBSERVED_MATCH`, or `OBSERVED_MISMATCH`.
- `symmetry_checks` is a verification trace, not a second source of ordinary pair
  results.

**Symmetry statuses:**

| Status | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`NOT_PERFORMED`** | No checks and no mechanism attestation |
| **`OBSERVED_MATCH`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty; every expected pair is covered by a `MATCH` check with `evidence_ref`; `symmetry_declaration ≠ SYMMETRIC` |
| **`OBSERVED_MISMATCH`** | At least one `MISMATCH` exists; `symmetry_declaration ≠ SYMMETRIC` |
| **`VERIFIED`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty; every expected pair is covered by a `MATCH` check with `evidence_ref`; `symmetry_declaration = SYMMETRIC` |
| **`VIOLATION`** | At least one `MISMATCH` exists; `symmetry_declaration = SYMMETRIC` |
| **`MECHANISM_ASSERTED`** | `expected_pairs` is non-empty; `pair_coverage_status = COVERED`; `predicate_execution_status = INVOKED`; `symmetry_declaration = SYMMETRIC`; `mechanism_ref` and `evidence_ref` bind to `evaluation_ref` and `expected_pairs` |
| **`INCONCLUSIVE`** | Checks were performed; no `MISMATCH`; coverage is partial or at least one comparison is `INCONCLUSIVE` |

When `expected_pairs` is empty, `symmetry_verification.status` MUST be `NOT_PERFORMED`; it cannot be `VERIFIED`, `OBSERVED_MATCH`, or `MECHANISM_ASSERTED` vacuously.

**Valid combinations:**

| `pair_order` | `symmetry_declaration` | Allowed `symmetry_verification.status` |
|---|---|---|
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `MECHANISM_ASSERTED`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `ASYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `OBSERVED_MATCH`, `OBSERVED_MISMATCH`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `UNORDERED_CANONICAL` | `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `OBSERVED_MATCH`, `OBSERVED_MISMATCH`, `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| `ORDERED` | `ASYMMETRIC` or `UNSPECIFIED` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `OBSERVED_MATCH`, `OBSERVED_MISMATCH`, `INCONCLUSIVE`; only `RULE_SELECTED`; ordered semantics OPEN |
| `ORDERED` | `SYMMETRIC` | `NOT_PERFORMED`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `MECHANISM_ASSERTED`, `INCONCLUSIVE`; only `RULE_SELECTED`; ordered semantics OPEN |

A single canonical evaluation of `(left, right)` cannot establish that
`(right, left)` produces the same result. `VERIFIED` requires full `MATCH` check
coverage. A mechanism guarantee is represented as `MECHANISM_ASSERTED`, not
`VERIFIED`; it is an attestation, not structural verification.

### 6.12 Structural invariants

| ID | Invariant |
|---|---|
| **E1** | No duplicate IDs within any single list |
| **E2** | `structural_candidates` contains only IDs present in the input set referenced by `input_set_ref` |
| **E3** | Context disposition facts are pairwise disjoint by `assessment_id` |
| **E4** | Every structural candidate has exactly one `ContextDispositionFact` |
| **E5** | `context_assessment_status = COMPLETE` implies all facts are `CONTEXT_APPLICABLE` or `CONTEXT_INAPPLICABLE`; `PARTIAL` implies at least one `CONTEXT_UNASSESSED` |
| **E6** | `considered` and `excluded_from_consideration` are disjoint subsets of the derived `context_applicable` set |

content.text:
Проверил и обработал комментарии к PR #63.

## Что было в комментариях

- **Gemini Code Assist:** 2 замечания — `pairKey` с неопределёнными `min`/`max`; type mismatch в `expected_pairs = terminal_pairs ⊎ ...`.
- **Два независимых adversarial review:** verdict `ACCEPT WITH OPEN ITEMS`, findings F-1…F-11 / F-01…F-08. Основные блокеры: ORDERED universe, состояние `UNSPECIFIED + all MATCH`, `PairKey`, E10, обязательность `predicate_ref`, overclaim `VERIFIED` через mechanism guarantee, `VIOLATION` при `UNSPECIFIED`, `RULE_SELECTED` scope, evidence refs.
- **SonarCloud:** Quality Gate passed.

## Что исправлено

Коммит `8c110ad` (влит в `main` merge-коммитом `037d6ec`):

- `pairKey` — explicit `compareIds` + injective `JSON.stringify`.
- E10 переписан в `PairKey`-множествах: `expectedKeys = terminalKeys ⊎ failedKeys ⊎ missingKeys`.
- `PAIRWISE_ALL_CONSIDERED` явно запрещён с `ORDERED`; `ORDERED` — только через `RULE_SELECTED` и остаётся OPEN.
- Семантика симметрии разделена: `OBSERVED_MATCH`, `OBSERVED_MISMATCH`, `VERIFIED`, `VIOLATION`, `MECHANISM_ASSERTED`, `INCONCLUSIVE`.
- `VERIFIED` требует полного `MATCH` coverage + `SYMMETRIC`; mechanism guarantee — отдельный `MECHANISM_ASSERTED`, только при полном coverage, attestation only.
- Top-level `predicate_ref` обязателен при configured predicate / непустых `pair_evaluations`.
- Evidence refs origin/structural/symmetry должны быть разными.
- `RULE_SELECTED` ограничен парами из `considered`; evidence binds rule version/input/output.
- `symmetry_checks`: `forward_status` соответствует canonical pair evaluation; `reverse_status` — trace-only, если reverse pair сам не expected.
- S19: terminal pair findings остаются authoritative; отсутствует только complete-coverage success claim.
- Добавлен provenance note и `O-PROV`; T-1 помечен как owner instruction.

Governance не менял: EP-2/BP-1 — PROPOSED, N2/N5 — PENDING SPEC AMENDMENT, D1–D6/N1–N11 не approved, Task 17/18 statuses не менялись.

## Статус PR

- PR: https://github.com/zaebee/federation-agents/pull/63
- Head: `037d6ec`
- `Format, lint, typecheck, test, build` — pass
- SonarCloud — pass
- **Entire Gates — fail только по approval gate:** “No reviewers have approved this trail”. Это ожидаемо: PR ждёт ревьюера, а не падает по коду.
- Merge не делал.

Ответил на оба Gemini-треда и оставил общий комментарий с перечнем исправлений.
